item.title: Development, Acceptance and Production Environments
item.description: Development, Acceptance and Production Environments Definition Layered environments Modern software processes deploy the same tech stack in several environments: development (Dev, also test), acceptance (Acc, also staging) and production (Prod).

item.title: Parameter Sharing
item.description: Parameter Sharing Definition Parameter sharing In deep MARL, all agents use the same set of parameter values in their neural networks: one policy or value network \theta for the whole team instead of one \theta_i per agent.

item.title: Policy Space Response Oracles (PSRO)
item.description: Policy Space Response Oracles (PSRO) Source: MARL book (Albrecht, Christianos and Schäfer, Ch 9, population-based training) and the AGAI mock midterm key; the AGAI lecture on deep MARL does not cover it.

item.title: Agent Modelling
item.description: Agent Modelling Definition Agent modelling An agent explicitly models the policies of the other agents, so that it can condition its own action selection on their predicted behaviour and adapt when that behaviour changes.

item.title: Containerization
item.description: Containerization Definition Container A container is a packaged application (code, interpreter, libraries, configuration) running as an isolated process on a host machine.

item.title: Docker
item.description: Docker Definition Docker Docker is the most widely used platform for containers: a Dockerfile describes how to build an image, the docker command-line tool builds, runs and inspects images and containers, and Docker Compose defines and starts several containers together.

item.title: GitFlow
item.description: GitFlow Definition GitFlow GitFlow is a git branching model with two long-living branches, main (the official release history) and develop (the integration branch for features), plus short-lived feature, release and hotfix branches.
